summary.one_liner: Chime is a free, open-source text editor for macOS (with iOS and visionOS support in progress), built from modular components and extensible through ChimeKit.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Chime as an editor for macOS, with iOS and visionOS support described as in the works. Listed features include completions, a command line tool, document/project-scoped search, editorconfig support, a file navigator, multiple cursors, semantic symbol information, structure highlighting, and textual/symbolic quick open. Syntax highlighting is described as three-phase: patterns, tree-sitter, and LSP. It also ships a Quick Look Preview extension, a Shortcuts extension for text highlighting, and UI theming. Bundled extensions for Clojure, Elixir, Go, Markdown, Python, Ruby, Rust, and Swift are listed. The README states the editor is mostly non-functional right now, and that the 3.0 version is an alpha; the stable 2.x version is closed-source.
use_cases: exploring a macOS code project with a file navigator
trying an experimental open-source macOS editor
how_to_run: Update User.xcconfig with your personal information
Build and run with Xcode (requires Xcode 26.4+ and macOS 26.2+)
notable: Three-phase syntax highlighting: patterns, tree-sitter, and LSP
